claims.sourceText: Schulgen, 'Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft', draft collection memorandum, 28 Oct 1947 (distributed 30 Oct 1947)
claims.text: Schulgen's collection memorandum instructed collectors to report on disc-type craft with 'extreme maneuverability and apparent ability to almost hover' and construction achieving 'extreme light weight.'

claims.nodeLabel: Schulgen Collection Memorandum: Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft
claims.sourceText: Schulgen draft collection memorandum, 1947, declassified text
claims.text: The document is titled 'Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft', signed by Brig. Gen. George F. Schulgen, Chief, Air Intelligence Requirements Division, dated 28 October 1947 and distributed 30 October 1947.

claims.nodeLabel: Schulgen Collection Memorandum: Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft
claims.sourceText: Schulgen collection memorandum, design origins section
claims.text: The memorandum frames the objects as potentially manned aircraft of Russian origin derived from German Horten brothers designs and asks for the Hortens' current whereabouts.

claims.nodeLabel: Schulgen Collection Memorandum: Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft
claims.text: 'Nuclear propulsion (atomic energy)' is listed among the propulsion systems collectors were to investigate.

claims.nodeLabel: Schulgen Collection Memorandum: Intelligence Requirements on Flying Saucer Type Aircraft
claims.sourceText: Schulgen collection memorandum, observable features section
claims.text: Collectors were directed to report on 'extreme maneuverability and apparent ability to almost hover', a 'relatively flat bottom with extreme light-reflecting ability', and an oval or disc plan form with a dome.
